question: After quotienting neural-network parameters by hidden-unit permutations, do independently trained networks occupy a common linearly connected loss valley, and can a task-informed permutation make the average of two nominally random initializations perform above chance before ordinary training?

key_findings.claim: The paper searches for a function-preserving hidden-unit permutation by matching layer activations with a maximum-weight bipartite assignment, then measures the loss barrier along the straight parameter interpolation.
key_findings.evidence: For each layer, activations of the two networks on a shared set of examples form two data-by-neuron matrices. Pairwise cosine similarity after the nonlinearity supplies assignment weights, and the Hungarian algorithm maximizes total matched similarity. The barrier is the maximum interpolation loss above the linear interpolation of endpoint losses.

key_findings.claim: For the tested fully connected classifiers, activation matching sharply reduces linear-interpolation barriers, and the residual barrier becomes visually negligible at sufficient width while increasing with depth or insufficient width.
key_findings.evidence: Fashion-MNIST networks are trained for five epochs with AdamW and then compared before and after permutation. Figure 2 reports single-network, vanilla-average, and permuted-average performance across widths and depths, with twice-standard-error bands over six seeds. The authors report the same qualitative pattern on MNIST and CIFAR-10 in Figures 6-7.

key_findings.claim: A permutation inferred from two trained descendants can be transported back to their initial weights, after which the midpoint of the two permuted initializations classifies above chance; averaging more aligned initializations further improves performance.
key_findings.evidence: Figure 3 applies the post-training activation permutation to saved initial parameters of a two-hidden-layer, width-2048 Fashion-MNIST MLP. The interpolation midpoint is reported substantially above chance, performance rises when more initializations are aligned to a reference and averaged, and permutations obtained after relatively few updates already reveal much of the effect. Figures 8-9 replicate the qualitative result on CIFAR-10 and MNIST.

key_findings.claim: The authors also construct useful permutations without completing network training, but this construction remains supervised and optimizer-informed rather than task-free.
key_findings.evidence: Appendix B minimizes a symmetrized dot product between a permuted initialization displacement and update directions computed from the loss. Vanilla gradients are said to be inadequate, so the reported method substitutes a FOOF update direction; it therefore consumes examples, labels through the loss, and a task-specific optimization signal even though it does not run the ordinary training trajectory.

anchors.section: Claim that permutations can be found without training
Appendix B, Equation 4 and FOOF construction

key_findings.claim: The tested convolutional networks retain a notable post-matching barrier, especially for learning rates near the edge of stability, and their aligned initializations do not show the fully connected networks' above-chance midpoint effect.
key_findings.evidence: Figure 4 compares small- and large-learning-rate CNN runs and the corresponding initialization interpolation. Across the simple convolution-plus-average-pooling stacks, datasets, and both AdamW and momentum SGD, the authors report larger residual barriers at large learning rates and chance-like averaged initializations. A CIFAR-10/AdamW replication appears in Figure 10.

key_findings.claim: Several implementation variants preserve the qualitative observations, but none turns the heuristic permutation search into a completeness test.
key_findings.evidence: Cosine versus Euclidean activation similarity and pre- versus post-nonlinearity features behave similarly; adding small rotations helps slightly, curved layerwise rotations hurt, and sequential weight matching is slightly worse. Orthogonal and Xavier initialization and mean-squared-error loss also preserve linear connectivity after permutation. The authors explicitly concede that a residual barrier in narrow networks could reflect a suboptimal assignment because exhaustive permutation search is infeasible.

anchors.section: Appendix C, failed second-order assignment search
Appendix D, feature, weight, and rotation variants

key_findings.claim: The title's apparent claim about random initialization is selection-conditioned: neither unselected endpoint is above chance, and the selected permutation can encode substantial information from future training or the labeled loss.
key_findings.evidence: The principal permutation is selected by matching activations after both models have learned the task and is only then applied retrospectively to stored initial weights. The alternative in Appendix B directly optimizes a loss-derived update criterion. With factorially many hidden-unit assignments, above-chance midpoint performance after this task-conditioned search does not establish that an ordinary random initialization, or a permutation chosen without task information, is predictive.

key_findings.claim: The experiments support low-barrier straight segments for sampled model pairs, not the universal conclusion that all SGD solutions share one loss valley or one approximately convex basin.
key_findings.evidence: A low sampled barrier after one permutation is valid instance-level evidence, but the paper evaluates a finite set of pairwise interpolations on small vision tasks. Conversely, a residual barrier cannot refute the existential conjecture because the assignment is heuristic. The initialization endpoints are themselves high-loss points, and pairwise straight-line connectivity does not establish that all aligned models jointly inhabit a common convex set.

anchors.section: Claim of direct confirmation and heuristic-search caveat
Appendix A, relation to nonlinear mode connectivity

key_findings.claim: The architecture and optimizer conclusions are exploratory because the fully connected models are only trained for five epochs with AdamW, while the CNN learning-rate comparison is deliberately conducted near instability and lacks a matched convergence analysis.
key_findings.evidence: The main fully connected protocol uses PyTorch-default AdamW for five epochs despite repeatedly framing endpoints as SGD solutions. For CNNs, the large-rate runs occasionally fail to converge, and the paper says the barrier is sensitive enough to training details to complicate width/depth comparisons. The appendix specifies batch size, initialization, activation, broad optimizer family, and CNN shapes but does not provide a complete per-figure schedule or a compute- and endpoint-quality-matched causal test of learning rate.

key_findings.claim: The appendix's written permutation-invariance derivation contains a dimension-ordering error, although the underlying hidden-unit symmetry is standard and repairable.
key_findings.evidence: Appendix E states that W_i has shape n_{i-1} by n_i but then left-multiplies W_i by the n_i by n_i matrix P_i^T and writes A_i = sigma(W_i A_{i-1}); these operations require the transposed convention W_i in R^{n_i by n_{i-1}} for column activations. Correcting that shape makes the displayed reparameterization dimensionally consistent.

method.core_idea: Remove the most obvious discrete parameter symmetry before diagnosing landscape connectivity: align corresponding hidden features across two independently initialized networks, permute one network without changing its function, and inspect straight-line interpolation both after training and retrospectively at initialization.
method.mechanism: Run two models independently; collect layer activations on shared data; solve one Hungarian assignment per hidden layer using cosine similarity; apply the induced row/column or channel permutations consistently across adjacent layers; and evaluate loss or accuracy along lambda theta_1 plus (1-lambda) theta_2. Saved initial weights receive the permutation inferred from their trained descendants. A separate initialization-only construction converts a symmetrized first-order loss criterion, using FOOF update directions, into another assignment problem. Width, depth, architecture, optimizer, learning rate, initialization, loss, and matching variants are swept empirically.
assumptions: Hidden-unit or channel permutations capture the function-preserving symmetry most relevant to the observed barriers.
Layerwise activation similarity on a finite shared sample is a useful surrogate for directly minimizing the maximum interpolation loss.
Independent layer assignments can be composed into a globally useful network permutation despite cross-layer dependencies.
A straight parameter segment with no empirical loss increase is adequate evidence that two endpoints occupy the same relevant valley.
Five-epoch AdamW endpoints in the fully connected experiments are representative of independently optimized solutions discussed under the broader label SGD.
The selected MNIST, Fashion-MNIST, CIFAR-10, MLP, and simple CNN settings reveal architecture-level rather than benchmark-specific behavior.
Test-set or held-out interpolation curves faithfully reflect the surrounding loss geometry rather than calibration or activation-scale artifacts.
Permutations selected from trained descendants may legitimately characterize their initializations even though the selection contains future task information.
A larger barrier at a larger learning rate reflects more diverse modes rather than unequal convergence, instability, or other changed endpoint statistics.

techniques.role: Aligns hidden units or channels by maximizing summed cosine similarity of their activation vectors.
Measures the maximum excess loss along a straight segment before and after a function-preserving reparameterization.
Applies a permutation inferred after training back to the corresponding saved random initialization.
Uses supervised optimizer update directions to search for an initialization permutation without completing ordinary training.
Contrasts when residual barriers disappear across MLP capacity and simple convolutional architectures.
Tests whether near-instability learning rates correlate with larger post-alignment CNN barriers.
Compares activation metrics, pre/post nonlinearities, weights, small rotations, and second-order assignment relaxations.

evaluations.setting: Fully connected Fashion-MNIST classifiers of varying width and depth, trained independently for five epochs with PyTorch-default AdamW
evaluations.metric: Accuracy or loss at the parameter average and maximum linear-interpolation loss barrier; Figure 2 reports twice the SEM over six seeds
evaluations.result: Activation permutation dramatically improves the average, with the residual barrier becoming visually negligible at sufficient width and worsening for narrower or deeper networks.
evaluations.baseline: Single trained network and vanilla, unpermuted weight averaging

evaluations.setting: Two-hidden-layer, width-2048 Fashion-MNIST MLPs with post-training permutations applied to saved initial parameters
evaluations.metric: Accuracy along the interpolation, especially at the midpoint, and accuracy after averaging increasing numbers of aligned initializations
evaluations.result: The aligned midpoint is reported significantly above the ten-class chance level, and averaging more aligned initializations improves it further.
evaluations.baseline: Unpermuted random-initialization average and the individual random endpoints

evaluations.setting: Initialization permutations obtained after different numbers of updates or directly through the symmetrized FOOF update-direction assignment
evaluations.metric: Accuracy of the averaged initial parameters
evaluations.result: Relatively little trajectory information is sufficient, and the direct supervised assignment is reported to achieve performance similar to the trained-descendant permutation.
evaluations.baseline: Permutation found only after the full five-epoch training run and vanilla-gradient matching, which the authors say does not work well

evaluations.setting: Simple convolutional stacks with channel widths k in {32, 64, 128, 256}, average pooling, and global-average-pooling readout across standard image datasets and optimizer choices
evaluations.metric: Post-permutation interpolation barrier under smaller versus near-instability learning rates and accuracy of averaged initializations
evaluations.result: Matching lowers the barrier but usually leaves a notable residual; larger learning rates yield larger barriers, and aligned initialization averages remain near chance.
evaluations.baseline: Unpermuted interpolation, smaller-learning-rate CNN training, and the fully connected initialization effect

evaluations.setting: MNIST and CIFAR-10 replications plus Kaiming-He, orthogonal, and Xavier initialization and cross-entropy versus mean-squared-error variants
evaluations.metric: Single-model, vanilla-average, and permuted-average performance before and after training
evaluations.result: The qualitative fully connected connectivity result persists across the reported datasets, initialization families, and losses, although vanilla averaging quality varies.
evaluations.baseline: Fashion-MNIST with Kaiming-He initialization and cross-entropy

limitations: The work is an OPT2022 workshop paper whose central conclusions are empirical; it neither proves the permutation-connectivity conjecture nor supplies a complete permutation-search certificate.
Residual barriers in narrow MLPs or CNNs cannot distinguish a genuinely different basin from failure of the layerwise Hungarian surrogate.
The phrase same loss valley is not given a topological definition and is operationalized only by one sampled straight interpolation under an empirical loss.
Above-chance initialization performance is conditioned on a permutation selected using trained descendants or labeled loss/update information, so it is not a task-free property of random draws.
The principal fully connected endpoints receive only five epochs of AdamW training, leaving endpoint convergence and the repeated SGD wording imperfectly aligned.

Architectural evidence is limited to MLPs and simple convolution/average-pooling stacks on MNIST-family and CIFAR-10 data; it does not cover normalization-heavy, residual, attention, or large-scale models.
Figure 2 reports six-seed uncertainty, but the initialization and CNN claims do not receive comparably clear confidence intervals, hypothesis tests, or multiplicity controls in the text.

The near-instability learning-rate comparison changes convergence reliability and likely endpoint calibration as well as mode diversity, without a matched-loss or matched-training-quality causal control.
The appendix omits a complete per-figure CNN schedule and does not report the exact sampling protocol for interpolation maxima in prose.
Activation scale and variance along interpolated deep networks are not controlled; later REPAIR work identifies variance collapse as a major reason alignment alone can leave a barrier.
Pairwise alignments are not tested for cycle consistency or simultaneous connectivity of three or more models, so they do not establish one shared approximately convex basin.
Only permutations and small rotation variants are considered, leaving positive rescalings, sign symmetries where applicable, and broader function-preserving transformations outside the quotient.
Appendix E reverses the stated weight-matrix dimensions relative to its multiplication convention, a repairable presentation error in the symmetry derivation.
failure_modes: Future-training leakage can make a retrospectively aligned initialization look intrinsically predictive when the permutation itself carries learned task structure.
A failed heuristic match can be mistaken for proof of disconnected modes, especially in narrow or convolutional networks.
A low barrier caused by width, calibration, or preserved activation statistics can be overinterpreted as evidence that SGD found the same semantic solution.
Pairwise low-loss segments can be mutually inconsistent, so averaging many models aligned independently to one reference may leave the alleged common basin.
Interpolation on finite train or test samples can miss off-sample functional disagreement and does not characterize the full connected component of parameter space.
Near-divergent learning rates can inflate barriers through poorer endpoint convergence or scale mismatch rather than through discovery of genuinely distinct modes.
Layerwise assignments may choose locally similar features that are globally incompatible across adjacent layers.
Activation matching requires representative shared data; distribution shift, restricted samples, or label-conditioned selection can change the inferred permutation.
Combining more selected initializations can increase the permutation search's information capacity, confounding ensemble-count effects with selection strength.
Claims derived from plain CNNs may reverse once normalization statistics are repaired or residual architecture symmetries are handled.
reusable_insights: Always quotient obvious function-preserving symmetries before using Euclidean parameter paths to diagnose whether independently trained networks differ.
Carry an alignment learned late in training back to earlier checkpoints as a diagnostic of when representational correspondence becomes identifiable.
Separate an initialization's raw performance from performance after a data-dependent combinatorial selection, and measure the information consumed by that selection.
Report both the full interpolation curve and the endpoint-adjusted barrier; midpoint accuracy alone can hide asymmetric endpoints or noncentral maxima.
Use width, depth, architecture, and learning-rate sweeps jointly because each can alter matching quality, activation statistics, and genuine solution diversity.
Add activation-moment repair and calibration controls before attributing an interpolation barrier to topology.
Test cycle consistency and joint convex-hull loss for multiple models rather than inferring a single basin from pairwise connections.
Treat a matching algorithm as a lower bound on achievable connectivity: success witnesses a path, while failure is not a disconnection certificate.
Compare weight-, activation-, and loss-aware objectives because they expose different assumptions about what corresponding neurons mean.
open_questions: How much labeled information, measured in bits or effective search complexity, is encoded by the permutation that makes random-initialization averaging predictive?
Can a permutation chosen on one task, data split, or domain make the same initialization average useful on genuinely held-out tasks without selection leakage?
Which part of the width effect comes from a larger permutation orbit, and which part would arise from width alone after activation calibration?
Can one design a tractable certificate or tight relaxation that distinguishes assignment failure from a genuine residual barrier?
Do simultaneous, cycle-consistent alignments place many independently trained models in one low-loss convex hull rather than merely connect selected pairs?
How do batch normalization, residual connections, attention heads, positive rescaling, and other symmetries change the initialization and CNN conclusions?
Does the large-learning-rate CNN effect survive controls matching endpoint loss, margin, calibration, weight norm, training compute, and stability?
Are aligned networks functionally similar under distribution shift, adversarial perturbations, and representation interventions even when their in-distribution interpolation barrier is small?
Can the direct initialization search be evaluated against label permutations, held-out-label selection, random assignments, and matched combinatorial search budgets?
What predicts whether alignment plus activation-moment repair is sufficient, and when genuinely nonlinear paths or additional capacity are necessary?

competitive_landscape.title: The Role of Permutation Invariance in Linear Mode Connectivity of Neural Networks
competitive_landscape.difference: Entezari et al. state the conjecture that motivates the reviewed paper and report evidence that many apparent barriers vanish after hidden-unit permutations. The reviewed work supplies a simple activation-matching witness, a systematic MLP width/depth study, the retrospective initialization result, and a CNN/learning-rate contrast rather than originating the conjecture.
competitive_landscape.source_version: ICLR 2022 conference paper, OpenReview forum dNigytemkL

competitive_landscape.title: Optimizing Mode Connectivity via Neuron Alignment
competitive_landscape.difference: Tatro et al. already align neurons from intermediate activations and jointly optimize permutations with simple learned connectivity curves, including adversarially robust models and a theoretical upper-bound analysis. The reviewed paper focuses on unlearned straight segments, a cheaper independent Hungarian match, and transporting the learned permutation back to initialization.

competitive_landscape.title: Model Fusion via Optimal Transport
competitive_landscape.difference: Singh and Jaggi align neurons with hard or soft optimal transport and demonstrate one-shot fusion across widths and non-IID data. Their objective is usable model fusion, whereas the reviewed paper uses hard feature matching primarily to test loss-landscape claims and uniquely examines aligned random initializations.

competitive_landscape.title: Git Re-Basin: Merging Models modulo Permutation Symmetries
competitive_landscape.difference: Ainsworth et al. independently develop weight matching, activation matching, and a straight-through estimator; demonstrate re-basing and merging including widened ResNets; and provide a finite counterexample. The reviewed paper's clearest additions are its systematic fully connected width/depth curves, CNN learning-rate dependence, and above-chance ancestral-initialization observation.
competitive_landscape.source_version: ICLR 2023 conference paper, OpenReview forum CQsmMYmlP5T

competitive_landscape.title: REPAIR: REnormalizing Permuted Activations for Interpolation Repair
competitive_landscape.difference: Jordan et al. show that alignment alone can leave a barrier because interpolated deep networks suffer activation-variance collapse, then repair preactivation moments. This supplies a concrete alternative explanation for the reviewed paper's CNN residual barriers and weakens any inference that those barriers necessarily mark genuinely distinct modes.
competitive_landscape.source_version: ICLR 2023 conference paper, OpenReview forum gU5sJ6ZggcX

competitive_landscape.title: Re-Basin via Implicit Sinkhorn Differentiation
competitive_landscape.difference: Pena et al. replace discrete, non-differentiable matching with an implicit-differentiation Sinkhorn re-basin module that can optimize task-specific objectives and support continual learning. It directly addresses the reviewed paper's acknowledged inability to know whether a residual barrier is due to a suboptimal permutation.

competitive_landscape.title: Analysis of Linear Mode Connectivity via Permutation-Based Weight Matching: With Insights into Other Permutation Search Methods
competitive_landscape.difference: Ito et al. argue empirically that connectivity is not explained merely by reducing parameter distance; weight and activation matching align dominant singular-vector directions that preserve model functionality. This supplies a spectral mechanism missing from the reviewed paper and compares activation matching directly with weight matching and straight-through search.
competitive_landscape.source_version: ICLR 2025 conference paper, corresponding to arXiv:2402.04051v5

competitive_landscape.title: Analyzing the Role of Permutation Invariance in Linear Mode Connectivity
competitive_landscape.difference: Zhan et al. formalize the width observation for two-layer ReLU teacher-student models: the modulo-permutation barrier exhibits double descent and decays at O(m^-1/2) when sufficiently wide, while learning-rate-driven sparsity changes the barrier. This turns two central empirical axes of the reviewed paper into a restricted but quantitative theory.

competitive_landscape.title: Linear Mode Connectivity between Multiple Models modulo Permutation Symmetries
competitive_landscape.difference: Ito et al. show that permutation methods designed for two models can fail to move many models into one convex low-loss basin, then introduce STE-MM and test pairwise barriers, merged loss, and Hessian trace. This directly exposes the gap between the reviewed paper's pairwise evidence and its language about a shared basin or averaging more than two initializations.

competitive_landscape.title: Do We Really Need Permutations? Impact of Model Width on Linear Mode Connectivity
competitive_landscape.difference: Ito et al. report that sufficiently widening models can produce linear connectivity even without permutations when softmax temperature is calibrated, and propose layerwise exponentially weighted connectivity as an explanation. This challenges the reviewed paper's implicit attribution of the width trend primarily to finding better permutations and highlights calibration as a missing control.
competitive_landscape.source_version: ICLR 2026 conference paper, OpenReview forum ll8GLAic7q

novelty_assessment.author_claim: The paper claims direct empirical confirmation of permutation-aware linear mode connectivity for sufficiently wide fully connected networks, the stronger discovery that suitably permuted random initializations already share a valley and average above chance, and contrasting evidence that CNNs—especially at large learning rates—occupy genuinely diverse modes.
novelty_assessment.evidence: Its evidence consists of activation-based Hungarian matching, straight interpolation plots across width/depth and architecture, retrospective application of trained permutations to saved initial weights, a supervised FOOF-based initialization search, and dataset, initialization, loss, optimizer, and learning-rate variants.
novelty_assessment.reviewer_inference: The most distinctive 2022 contribution is the retrospective initialization experiment plus the MLP-versus-CNN and learning-rate comparison. Activation/neuron alignment and permutation-aware connectivity already had close precedents, and Git Re-Basin was concurrent. The universal single-valley and genuinely-distinct-CNN interpretations are stronger than the evidence: selection leaks task information, matching failure is not a disconnection certificate, and later REPAIR, spectral, multi-model, theoretical-width, and calibration results identify important alternative mechanisms and missing controls.

reviewer_notes: All 18 cached pages of arXiv:2209.07509v2 were read, including experimental appendices and references; the integrity index reports usable text on every page. Claims are anchored to PDF pages rather than inferred from the abstract. The audit separates three notions that the paper sometimes blends: existence of one low-barrier straight segment for a sampled pair, membership in a topological loss-valley component, and simultaneous membership of many models in one approximately convex basin. It also treats above-chance initialization performance as task-conditioned because the permutation is selected by trained descendants or labeled-loss update directions. Competing primary sources were checked on 2026-08-23 through OpenReview, official NeurIPS/CVPR/PMLR proceedings, and arXiv; the panel includes foundational, concurrent, corrective, mechanistic, theoretical, multi-model, and 2026 calibration/width work.
